PtrsLong05D778.name: Load level: pointers, start position, layout
summary: Entered by JSL $05D796 from the level load code (game mode 'prepare level') after the overworld or a screen exit chose the level.
Works out the level number ([$0E]/[$0F], [$13BF] translevel): from the screen exit table [$19B8] when [$141A] is set, otherwise from the
overworld position ($7E:D000 map) or [$0109]. Secondary exits ([$1B93]) take level, Mario start and layer positions from the $05F800+ tables.
Then loads the layer 1/2 data pointers [$65]/[$68], the sprite data pointer [$CE], the level header settings, Mario's start position,
scroll settings and the midway point entry. Some tilesets get a fixed start room (PtrsLong05D766/05D778, sprites at $07:C3EE).
Translevel $24 (Chocolate Island 2) re-entries pick an alternate layout via CODE_05DAEF. The first rows are the layer 2 pointer table
for the start rooms (bank byte $FF = layer 2 background from bank $0C, probably), followed by two small tables and the code.

PtrsLong05DAFF.name: Pointer table: Chocolate Island 2 layout choosers
summary: Long pointers used by ExecutePtrLong, indexed by layer 1 header byte 4 bits 7-6 (0-2).

ChocIsld2Layer1.name: Table: Chocolate Island 2 layer 1 data
summary: Layer 1 data pointers (low 16 bits; bank unchanged), indexed by X set in CODE_05DB3E/DB6E/DB82. Entries 7 and above are for the timer variant.

ChocIsld2Sprites.name: Table: Chocolate Island 2 sprite data
summary: Sprite data pointers (bank $07), same indexing as ChocIsld2Layer1.

ChocIsld2Layer2.name: Table: Chocolate Island 2 layer 2 data
summary: Layer 2 pointers; all nine point to $0C:DF59, so layer 2 never changes.

s05DBAC.name: Force screen exit to level $00 or $C8
summary: Sets the screen exit table entry [$19B8] of Mario's current screen to $00 ([$1B95] clear) or $C8 ([$1B95] set), and increments [$141A]
so the level is loaded as a screen-exit entry. Purpose of the flags is not fully clear (probably Yoshi wings / bonus entries).

s05DBC9.name: Data: lives counter stripe image
summary: Template for the lives counter stripe image; the first 9 bytes are copied to the $7F:837D buffer by CODE_05DBF2.

s05DBF2.name: Queue lives counter stripe image
summary: Builds a stripe image in $7F:837D that writes the current player's lives + 1 as one or two digit tiles at VRAM $5088 (BG3, overworld).
Called from the overworld load code (e.g. $00A15A) right after the border image.
Includes CODE_05DC3A: divide A by 10 by repeated subtraction; returns X = tens, A = ones.
